bull.b: Sustained gross margins near 68% and strong net margins indicate durable product-level pricing power and cost structure advantages in high-speed SerDes and optics. These margins support robust cash generation, reinvestment for R&D, and improve resilience to cyclical semiconductor demand swings.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and conservative balance sheet
bull.b: Large operating cash flows and substantial cash balances provide long-term financial flexibility to fund R&D, capital-lite expansion, and M&A (e.g., Dust Photonics). Low leverage and positive FCF reduce refinancing risk and support multi-year product ramp funding without dilutive capital raises.

bull.t: Strategic optics portfolio and inorganic buildout
bull.b: Adding silicon-photonics and optics IP via Dust Photonics materially expands addressable market and vertical stack presence. The combined optics roadmap (SiPho PICs, DSPs, ZeroFlap) creates multi-year revenue levers and sticky design wins that raise barriers for competitors in hyperscale interconnects.

bear.b: Heavy revenue reliance on a few customers creates durable execution risk: single-customer ordering patterns can cause quarter-to-quarter volatility, amplify negotiation leverage, and make scaling optics revenue and multi-customer diversification crucial to sustain forecasted growth.

Dependence on advanced process nodes and constrained supplier capacity can limit ability to meet demand for next-gen optical and SerDes products. Persistent node scarcity or vendor allocation shifts could delay customer ramps, raising structural execution risk beyond quarter-to-quarter timing.

bear.t: Timing uncertainty for optical and 200G ramps
bear.b: The company’s multi-year growth thesis relies on a back-half optical inflection and later 200G adoption. If customer deployment timing slips, revenue and margin expansion tied to optics could be pushed out, pressuring multi-year targets and making execution timing a structural risk for forecasts.
